exposure: Fetal echocardiographic (FE) assessment parameters (foramen ovale, atrial septal excursion, branch pulmonary artery pulsatility index (PA PI), middle cerebral artery (MCA) PI, cardiac output)
outcome: Requirement for emergency balloon atrial septostomy (e-BAS)
cohort: Thirty fetuses with transposition of the great arteries (TGA) who underwent standard and AMH-enhanced fetal echocardiographic assessments.
finding: A pulmonary artery pulsatility index (PA PI) change <=15% in response to acute maternal hyperoxygenation (AMH) was associated with postnatal hypoxia due to persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn (PPHN), while specific changes in right and combined cardiac output and reduced middle cerebral artery (MCA) resistance with AMH were observed in those who did not require e-BAS.
followup_time: Up to 2 hours after birth (for e-BAS assessment)
gest_age: Fetal assessments performed at 34.6 weeks' gestation (interquartile range, 34.6-35.6)
